$meta.readThisFirst: This is the APP-level primary navigation (blue rail on the far left of every page). It is DISTINCT from, and sits to the LEFT of, the record-level grey Profile Side Navigation (profile-side-navigation.json). Singh, 2026-09-04: complete all pending Primary-navigation tasks and verify each measurement (spacing + margin) forensically. Per his standing rule the behavior + purpose blocks are mandatory. The Figma structure timed out on the whole-frame get_design_context (known Figma-MCP stall) so it was measured piece-by-piece from metadata geometry + small-node design contexts — the forensic spacing map is in geometry.spacingMap.

purpose: The app's primary navigation — the blue rail on the far left of every page that moves the user between the top-level areas of the product (dashboard, clients, caregivers, scheduling, billing, reports…). It carries the company logo (a shortcut home), a collapse toggle to reclaim horizontal space, the section links, and the copyright. It is the OUTERMOST navigation layer: the grey Profile Side Navigation (per record) and the page tabs live to its right.

selectedContrast.value: White text/icon on sidebar/ring (#2499ff) is ≈3.0:1 — passes for LARGE text / UI components (3:1) but NOT the 4.5:1 normal-text bar. The nav label is 14px Medium = normal text. FLAG T3 — confirm the selected highlight is intended, or darken the ring for the selected row.

focusVisible.value: Every link + the toggle needs a visible focus ring. Uses a WHITE ring (--sidebar-text, inset offset -2) — DISTINCT from the --sidebar-ring selected fill, so focus stays visible even on a Selected row (WCAG 2.4.7). Never reuse --sidebar-ring for the focus outline (that would be invisible on the selected row).

defects: T1 — RESOLVED 2026-09-08. Figma now has 3 Hover variants (27364:6859 / 27364:7900 / 27364:7908) binding surface/brand-hover, drawn by the Figma-AI lane after the 2026-09-04 measurement. The kit's ADDED translucent-white hover is replaced by var(--surface-brand-hover). The token choice itself is defective — see T7.

T7 — HOVER TOKEN FAILS CONTRAST IN 4 OF 5 MODES (measured 2026-09-08 from the Aug-24 export). The Hover variants bind surface/brand-hover — a brand-SURFACE hover, not a sidebar token — so it does not co-vary with sidebar/text: text/icon contrast on the hover fill is Light 5.72:1 ✓, Dark Theme 1.16:1 ✗, High Contrast 1.10:1 ✗ (white on #F1F5F9), HC Light text 1.38:1 ✗ / icon 1.00:1 ✗ (icon is the same colour as the fill — invisible), Warm Dark 1.66:1 ✗. No existing sidebar/* token works in all five modes either: accent-bg and secondary-bg are tuned for the grey profile sidebar (Light 1.10 / 1.05), ring fails Light 2.97 / HC 1.92 / Warm 1.24, primary-bg is the rail itself. PROPOSED FIX — an ADD, allowed under the Agency naming lock (C360-44253 #622188 rule 4): a new token sidebar/primary-hover with per-mode values ≥4.5:1 against sidebar/text, and re-bind the three Hover variants to it. Requires the owner's ruling on the values and a Figma-AI re-bind; until then the kit follows Figma (var(--surface-brand-hover)) and carries this warning.

T2 — LOGO HEADER HAS NO TOKEN. It is white (#ffffff, RAW) sitting on the blue rail, with a RAW translucent hairline rgba(51,74,101,0.1). Neither binds a token. If the design system wants the logo header themeable, it needs a sidebar-surface / on-primary token; today it is two RAW values.

T3 — SELECTED CONTRAST. White 14px label on sidebar/ring (#2499ff) ≈ 3.0:1 in Light — below the 4.5:1 normal-text bar. Either accept it as a UI-component highlight (3:1 met) or darken the selected row's blue. Design-owner call. EXTENDED 2026-09-08 (all modes, sidebar/text on sidebar/ring): Light 2.97:1, Dark 4.04:1, High Contrast 1.92:1 ✗ (white on yellow-500 #EAB308 — fails even the 3:1 component bar), HC Light 13.17:1 ✓, Warm Dark 1.24:1 ✗. The HC and Warm Dark selected states need the owner's attention as much as the hover does.

T4 — the icon set 'priamry side nav icons' (10883:20899, 41 variants, note the 'priamry' typo) supplies every nav icon at 24px; individual icon↔section mapping is NOT enumerated here — bind per section when the nav is populated.
T5 — legacy token name fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 bound on the labels (same system-wide legacy-name cleanup). The kit uses semantic vars.
T6 — layer-name typo 'priamry' appears in the icon set and its instances; cosmetic, flag to Figma AI.
